raw_response:
Alright, let me think through this year's plan for my 5 mu.

---

Five mu isn't much — my wife and I can handle most of it ourselves, especially since two of the kids are grown and the youngest is still in school. My older son works in town most of the year, sends money home, but comes back to help with wheat harvest and maize planting because that week is crazy busy. You can't do it alone.

I've been doing wheat-maize for as long as I've been farming. Twenty-five years. I know this land. The soil here is okay — not the best in the village, but not bad either. My neighbor Old Wang on the plot next to mine gets maybe 480-500 kg/mu of wheat in a good year, and I usually get close to that, sometimes a bit less because my plot has a low spot that waterlogs if it rains hard in May.

**Wheat (October to June):**
I'll plant in mid-October like always, right after I clear the maize stubble. I use the improved variety the co-op sells — Jimai something, I forget the number, but it's what most people around here use. Maybe 15 kg seed per mu, around 5 yuan per kg.

Fertilizer — the extension guy came through last autumn and said 15 kg N per mu is enough, but honestly I do a bit more. Around 18 kg N total. I put down compound fertilizer (diammonium phosphate, the 15-15-15 stuff) before planting — about 40 kg per mu as base — and then topdress urea at jointing in March, maybe 15 kg per mu. If the crop looks yellow I might add a little more at booting, but usually I don't. Too much and the wheat lodges, I learned that the hard way about ten years ago.

Irrigation — I'll water three times. Once before winter to help it survive the cold, once at jointing (most important one, can't skip it), and once at grain filling if it's dry. Pumping from the well costs money — electricity and the time standing there — so I don't do extra unless I have to. If spring rain is good, I might skip the grain-filling one.

Pesticide — I spray herbicide once in spring for broadleaf weeds, and I watch for aphids at heading. If I see them I'll spray, if not I won't. Fungicide only if scab shows up, which is maybe one year in three.

Expected yield: around 450 kg/mu. That's my normal.

**Maize (June to October):**
Right after wheat harvest in June, I have to plant maize within three or four days. No tillage — I just direct-seed into the stubble with a no-till planter I hire from the co-op, costs about 30 yuan per mu including seed. This is the only way with such a tight window. The hired machine does it in half an hour for my whole plot.

I use hybrid seed, Zhengdan or whatever the shop is pushing that year, around 40 yuan per mu for seed. More expensive than wheat seed but you can't save hybrid.

Fertilizer — I use less on maize than wheat. Maybe 15 kg N per mu total. Base fertilizer with the seed at planting, and one topdress at the big trumpet stage (around V10) with urea. Summer rain usually does most of the watering for me. I only irrigate maize if we get a real dry spell in July or August — usually once, sometimes not at all.

Pesticide — I spray for armyworm if I see them, and sometimes for borers. One herbicide application after emergence.

Expected yield: around 480 kg/mu if the rain comes right.

**What I'm thinking about this year:**
Fertilizer prices have been going up and down. I'll buy in the off-season if the price is good. And I'm keeping some cash back in case the wife's mother needs medicine again — that's the kind of thing you have to plan for. You can't put every yuan into the field.
